newsitem.title: USA: Conoco acquisition fuels expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: Conoco acquisition fuels expansion plans.

text.p: Conoco Inc. on Friday acquired producing south Texas natural gas fields for $900 million as it moved to double the value of the company over the next five years, executives and analysts said.
The fields in the south Texas Lobo Trend hold proven and estimated reserves of 2.7 trillion cubic feet of natural gas, Conoco Executive Vice President Rob McKee said.
"We're on a sigificant kind of a growth path here within Conoco," said McKee, who heads the Houston-based company's global exploration and production operations.

Although rumours continue to swirl about the possibility DuPont Co. will spin off its energy subsidiary, the acquisition -- Conoco's largest ever -- shows they are not neglecting the core energy business, analysts said.

"I think it just gives them more good reserves in the areas where they already are very, very strong -- in natural gas production in the United States," said Theodore Semegran, a Brown Brothers Harriman & Co. analyst.
As part of its expansion, Conoco plans to add a power business and grow its core exploration and production activities beyond the United States and Western Europe.

The company through acquisitions and exploitation of existing assets plans to increase the market value of its exploration and production operation to $15.5 billion in 2000 from $10 billion in 1995, analysts said.
In the south Texas fields, Conoco will invest $1 billion over the next five years to more than double its current 800 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of North American production, McKee said.

"We intend to take the production in the total Lobo area from about 250 (mmcfd) up to about 800 (mmcfd) over the coming five years. It's actually closer to 900 (mmcfd) by the time we get this five-year programme in place," McKee said.

Conoco's newly acquired reserves in the Lobo trend are relatively long-lived, with an estimated reserve to production life of 30 years, far longer than the Wilmington, Del.-based company's current nine-year average, he said.

The producing fields and a 1,110-mile pipeline system were sold for $1.1 billion by TransTexas Gas Corp. to intermediary First Intercontinental Leasing Trust, which in turn sold the fields and pipeline to Conoco and retained certain other assets valued at $200 million, the companies said.

For TransTexas, the deal cuts its heavy debt load and allows the Houston-based company to boost its investment in south Texas gas fields, including the hot Bob West north and Wharton County plays, spokesman Simon Ward said.
"It will essentially allow us to de-leverage our balance sheet and focus on our new development efforts," he said.
DuPont stock rose 37.5 cents to $108.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
